name: Air Fryer Shrimp Tacos with Lime Cabbage Slaw

components.name: Seasoned Shrimp

ingredients.name: Taco seasoning or ground paprika, cumin and garlic blend

steps: Pat the peeled shrimp dry, toss with oil, garlic, seasoning and salt, then chill while making the slaw.
Preheat air fryer to 182 C. Spread shrimp in one layer and cook for about 5-7 minutes, shaking halfway, until opaque and centre reaches 63 C.
Pack tortillas, shrimp, slaw and sauce separately. Reheat shrimp gently and assemble just before serving; raw slaw and sauce do not freeze well.

components.name: Corn Tortillas
steps: Heat tortillas briefly in a dry pan or wrapped under gentle steam, then divide two tortillas and a quarter of shrimp among each serving.

components.name: Lime Slaw & Sauce
steps: Toss shredded cabbage, red onion and coriander with 45 ml lime juice; keep the slaw in sealed cold containers.
Whisk yogurt, light mayo, 20 ml lime and hot sauce into a separate smooth dressing.

notes: Draft — needs Mirna review: not kitchen-tested yet; macros and cooked yields are estimates.
Air-fryer shrimp cooking method and slaw/dressing sourced from Skinnytaste; quantities adapted to four protein-rich full dinners.
Planning: Secondary stovetop optional for tortilla warming.
Freezer: cooked shrimp can freeze; tortillas can freeze; raw cabbage slaw and yogurt dressing NOT freezer-friendly
Dietary: Shellfish, milk, egg if mayonnaise used; corn tortillas may contain wheat depending on brand.

Refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 32°C) in shallow containers at 4°C or colder, for 3–4 days at most, and follow the shorter seafood limit above. Cook fish and shellfish to 63°C and reheat leftovers to at least 74°C.

flags.shelfLife: Shrimp — plan for days 1-3; slaw and dressing don't freeze.

preservationAndReheating: Refrigerate cooked food promptly in shallow covered containers. Target within 2 hours, or 1 hour when ambient temperature exceeds 32 C.
Refrigerate at 4 C or below for 3-4 days maximum; for many fish and shrimp dishes, prioritize eating within 1-2 days for quality and freeze later-week cooked portions promptly.

Cook fish and crustaceans to 63 C (145 F) or applicable local food-safety standard, and reheat cooked leftovers to 74 C. For crab cakes containing egg binder and purchased cooked crab, reheat to 74 C.
When recipe includes rice, cool rapidly and refrigerate promptly; do not leave cooked rice at room temperature.
Freeze in suitable airtight food-safe containers. Defrost in refrigerator, not on counter. Re-crisp breading in an air fryer when possible.
Do not freeze fresh avocado, uncooked tomato/cucumber/cabbage salad, or mayonnaise/yogurt-based dressing unless kitchen-tested separately.
Freezer suitability here describes expected eating quality, not laboratory validated shelf life.
